concept: Backstage monochrome portrait at a lit stage edge
creativeDirection: Editorial location photography in a real backstage theatre space, using one cast portrait anchored by a recognisable concert-stage environment and a few quiet physical motifs from other sleeves.
scene: A worn indoor theatre backstage opens directly onto the side edge of a small stage during setup, with cables, mic stands, a floor wedge, a circular wall light, heavy drapery, and a warm red-orange glow spilling from the performance area into a cooler worklit prep space. The black-and-white man from source 4 stands near the stage edge at three-quarter length, posed with the calm, slightly turned close-portrait attitude of his sleeve, his dark clothing crisp against pale painted walls and curtains. Around him, the stage world supplies the main environment, while a large retro desktop computer sits powered off on a road case, a white bird emblem is painted small on a flight case, and a pair of gold lion finials cap two short posts by the drape.

elements.element: the indoor concert-stage setting itself: side-stage view with microphones, instruments, circular wall light, coloured spotlights, drapery, and red-magenta performance glow
the man from reference image 4, standing at three-quarter length with his slightly turned, close-portrait pose and dark clothing
a retro desktop computer at an angle on a black road case, screen dark and blank
a small white winged-bird emblem painted on a backstage flight case
two subtle gold lion finials on short stanchions beside the stage drape
amber-brown industrial wear and scuffed collage-like surface tones in the backstage walls and cases
stone-grey and silver tonal restraint in the room’s surfaces and hardware

prompt: Eye-level medium-close view in a real indoor theatre backstage beside the edge of a small performance stage, the camera close enough for a clear three-quarter-length portrait, with pale scuffed walls, heavy dark drapery, mic stands, cables, a floor wedge, instruments partly visible, and one circular wall light, the stage beyond spilling warm red, orange, and magenta light into a cooler worklit prep area. The man from reference image 4 is the primary subject, standing at his own scale near the stage edge in dark clothing, shoulders and torso visible, face turned slightly toward camera exactly in the calm close-portrait attitude of his sleeve, properly lit and sharply focused. Build the location from reference image 1 as a believable side-stage concert environment with coloured spotlights, circular light detail, and live-performance equipment. Include as smaller supporting details a retro desktop computer from reference image 8 sitting at an angle on a black road case with its screen powered off and blank, a small white winged-bird emblem from reference image 7 painted on a backstage flight case, and two understated gold lion finials from reference image 7 topping short posts beside the curtain. Let reference image 6 inform the amber-brown industrial wear and distressed surface character of the backstage materials, and reference image 5 inform the cooler stone-grey hardware and tonal restraint. Photographic realism, crisp editorial location photography, no collage look, no text, no extra people, no images of faces on any screen or surface. Compose as one cohesive backstage moment with the cast figure dominant and the support motifs only noticed on a second look. Clean, bright, readable lighting with warm stage spill from one side and practical worklights lifting the face. Palette of black, white, grey, red, orange, magenta, gold, and yellow; intimate, theatrical, poised mood. Reference map for people (the album images are attached in this numbered order): reference image 4 shows one man in a close portrait wearing dark clothing. Copy each of these faces directly from that numbered reference image - same face, bone structure, hair, expression, and styling - rather than drawing a new person from the description. Nobody from reference images 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 appears in the picture: use those images only for colour, setting, and objects, and add no figures, faces, or silhouettes from them. Hard constraints (override any conflicting source material): Create a single cohesive 16:9 image, not a grid, contact sheet, row of covers, or collage of separate panels. Do not reproduce the album sleeves as framed thumbnails, posters, record covers, or pictures on a screen, monitor, or television. A sleeve's abstract graphics, shapes, patterns, and colours may be painted onto the walls, doors, floor, or objects of the place as part of its decoration, without any lettering. Show no sleeve's faces, heads, or figures as a picture, mural, display, sign, relief, or silhouette anywhere; transform the sleeves' non-text visual motifs into one original composition. Include no readable text or lettering of any kind: no words, letters, numbers, code, glyphs, captions, titles, logos, watermarks, labels, or signage. Feature only adults and avoid gore, wounds, body horror, medical or anatomical imagery, blank or milky eyes, nudity, sexual content, weapons, and hate symbols; reinterpret any sensitive source motif abstractly. When a source includes a person, closely match their visible appearance and likeness to the reference image, preserving recognisable facial features, hair, skin tone, clothing, and styling, and their apparent age: every person is shown as the adult they are on the sleeve, never younger, smoothed, or more boyish or girlish. Keep each reference person in the pose, expression, and gaze the sleeve shows, and keep every identifiable face sharp, lit, unobscured, and in focus: no motion blur, long-exposure smearing, steam, fog, shadow, crowding, or shallow depth of field over a reference person's face. Expose the image cleanly whatever the light: every person's face well lit and readable, shadows that hold detail, and clear colour, with no murky underexposure, crushed blacks, heavy film grain, digital noise, or dust-and-scratches texture. Add no incidental plants: no flowers, potted plants, planters, climbing vines, ivy, hanging foliage, hedges, lawns, flower beds, or greenery framing the edges or carpeting the floor, unless the description above explicitly asks for that plant as part of a source motif or the year treatment. Dress the scene with the materials of the place itself - stone, metal, concrete, wood, fabric, glass, water, equipment - rather than vegetation. Everyone in the picture is photographed in the same place, at the same moment, under the same light as the rest of the scene, in full colour and with the same lens and grain: do not carry over a sleeve's own backdrop, studio lighting, backlit flare, monochrome, colour cast, or print texture onto the person. Each person stands inside the scene at the scale of the space around them, never as an oversized cropped head or bust looming at the edge of the frame over a distant scene, and never washed in red, blue, or other coloured light. Depict each identifiable reference person only once in the entire composition; do not repeat or clone them as another figure, reflection, mirror portrait, poster, billboard, screen, photograph, painting, silhouette, or background face. The only exception is repetition visibly intrinsic to one source cover: keep that repetition within that single source motif and do not echo the person elsewhere. The only people anywhere in the image are the reference people named in the reference map, and of those only the ones whose faces are clearly visible in their reference. Add no one else: no extra band members, musicians, staff, bystanders, passers-by, crowd, audience, background or out-of-focus figures, and no hands, arms, legs, or shadows of unseen people. Never complete a person who is hidden, cropped, turned away, blurred, or only partly visible in a reference with an invented face or body - leave that person out entirely. Photograph the reference people from roughly eye level, at three-quarter length or closer, in the near or middle ground, so each of their faces is large, sharp, and clearly recognisable in the final frame: never from directly above, and never as small distant figures.
